observed_result.criterion: With fallback and connection reuse disabled and only the marker key offered: fresh authentication fails before enrollment, succeeds (exactly one new Accepted line with the marker fingerprint) after the marker line is added alongside existing access, and fails after removal; existing access survives; removal by marker preserves every unrelated byte and a concurrent administrator edit; seed restored. Fail: any deviation.
observed_result.summary: Observed on fixture enroll: the verification config offered only the marker key (identitiesonly yes, no ControlMaster/ControlPath, publickey only, password/kbd off, dedicated agent). Marker-only fresh login before enrollment rc 255. Marker key appended alongside existing entries by CAS + atomic rename (after-add bytes = preimage + marker line). Marker-only fresh login rc 0 with exactly 1 new Accepted line with the marker fingerprint (1 key offered). Existing admin access still worked. A concurrent administrator append landed (rc 0). Removal of the marker line only (rc 0): after-remove bytes = preimage + the concurrent line (9 -> 10 lines), marker absent. Marker-only login afterwards rc 255. Concurrent line removed; seed sha256 restored, enroll:600, no temp files. Verdict pass.

limitations: OpenSSH mechanism evidence only: host client /usr/bin/ssh (OpenSSH_10.3p1, LibreSSL 3.3.6, macOS) against sshd (OpenSSH_10.0p2 Debian-7+deb13u4, OpenSSL 3.5.6 7 Apr 2026) in disposable Docker fixture containers. No Heimdall code exists or ran; this is not evidence of Heimdall behavior.

Not desktop-lock, sleep, logout, reboot or secure-store evidence: the dedicated agents are plain ssh-agent processes in an unlocked session started by the harness. Lock continuity remains open (owner-run probes).
Single machine: macOS 27.0 arm64 with Docker Desktop (linux VM). No native Windows/WSL or Linux-host evidence. The openssh-server package version is observed, not pinned (apt floats at image build).
Fixture sshd sets PerSourcePenalties no, unlike the OpenSSH 10 default.
Requirement IDs are listed for traceability; this record is not by itself evidence that any product requirement is met (tests/evidence/README.md).
